svg.title: NATS JetStream Flow: one cold contract, two intake paths
svg.desc: ConsumerContext pull and JetStream push converge on bounded Flow<Message>; acknowledgement, retry, and connection policy remain caller-owned.
svg.text: NATS JetStream Flow: one cold contract, two intake paths
ConsumerContext pull and JetStream push converge on bounded Flow<Message>; acknowledgement, retry, and connection policy remain caller-owned.
Read the sequence from left to right, then follow the branch frames
Flow<Message> · JetStreamSubscription · IterableConsumer · manual ack/nak/term
COLD
collect creates the handle
No subscription or IterableConsumer exists before
collection.
BOUNDED
capacity + pending limits
Finite channel and pending ceilings fail closed
when state cannot be trusted.
MANUAL
ack · nak · term stay outside
PublishAck confirms storage; business completion
is a caller decision.
Cold collection → bounded delivery → caller policy → cleanup
Numbered message lanes · lifelines · activation bars · chronological branch frames
Caller / collector
ack · nak · term policy
cold Flow<Message>
single bounded contract
NATS adapter
owns only its handle
JetStream / consumer
server delivery + state
1 · Declare a cold Flow
JetStream.consumeAsFlow(...) or ConsumerContext.consumeAsFlow(...)
The caller receives a Flow<Message> value; no subscription, IterableConsumer, or server pull starts before collection.
Guardrail · Cold collection is not a hot/shared stream. The same Flow instance rejects concurrent collection.
Next · Collect the value to create exactly one adapter-owned intake handle.
No auto-ack · no hidden connection ownership
2 · Collection opens the adapter handle
collect → runInterruptible(Dispatchers.IO)
Push creates a JetStreamSubscription; pull creates an IterableConsumer through iterate(effectiveOptions).
Guardrail · The adapter may clean up only handles it created; the injected connection and durable policy remain
caller-owned.
Next · Feed either handle into the same channelFlow.buffer(capacity) contract.
Push: subscribe · Pull: iterate
3 · Pull and push converge
nextMessage(receiveTimeout) → send(message)
Both adapters poll with a finite receiveTimeout and send Message values through one cold channelFlow.
Guardrail · Blocking receive runs on Dispatchers.IO and is interrupted by coroutine cancellation instead of being
abandoned.
Next · Apply independent message and byte ceilings before more values can queue.
One Flow contract · two transport-specific handles
4 · Keep intake finite
capacity 1..1,024 · pending ≤ 65,536 messages · pending ≤ 64 MiB
The Flow buffer is bounded. Pull batchSize is normalized to min(options.batchSize, capacity + 1); push reads pending
limits back.
Guardrail · byte-only pull batches are rejected because a message-count bound cannot be proven at the same time.
Next · Deliver each Message; acknowledgement remains outside the adapter.
Default push pending: 1,024 messages · 16 MiB
5 · Deliver without inventing policy
emit(Message)
The collector receives a Message and decides what successful business processing means.
Guardrail · The adapter never calls ack(), nak(), or term(); PublishAck only confirms server storage, not business
completion.
Next · Caller chooses ack, nak, term, or leaves the message unacknowledged.
Manual acknowledgement boundary
6 · Caller acknowledges success
business work → message.ack()
After downstream work succeeds, the caller sends ack to the JetStream consumer according to its own policy.
Guardrail · An ack is a caller decision and can fail independently of Flow delivery; the library does not checkpoint
business state.
Next · A durable consumer records the acknowledgement; continue until the next message or terminal lifecycle signal.
Caller-owned: ack()
ALT · retryable failure → nak or no ack → redelivery
7 · Nak or unack makes redelivery visible
message.nak() / ack wait expires → redelivery
A retryable failure uses nak, or the caller may leave the message unacknowledged until the durable consumer redelivers
it.
Guardrail · Redelivery is at-least-once. The adapter does not deduplicate side effects or promise exactly-once
processing.
Next · The caller must make downstream work idempotent or apply deduplication before accepting the replay.
ALT · retryable failure → nak / no ack
ELSE · pending drop / unreadable state → typed failure
8 · Push drop becomes a typed failure
droppedCount ↑ → NatsConsumerFlowException
If the push pending queue drops messages, the adapter observes droppedCount and fails instead of presenting a clean
but incomplete Flow.
Guardrail · Pending-limit read-back mismatch and observation failures also fail closed with NatsConsumerFlowException.
Next · The caller decides retry, backoff, and deduplication after the adapter closes its own handle.
ELSE · drop or unverifiable state → FAILED
LOOP · collect again → a fresh adapter handle
9 · Cancellation closes owned handles
cancel → interrupt receive → close / unsubscribe
Collector cancellation interrupts nextMessage and enters NonCancellable + Dispatchers.IO cleanup for the
adapter-created handle.
Guardrail · CancellationException is rethrown; cleanup does not close the caller-owned connection or invent a retry.
Next · Finish with cancellation after unsubscribe or IterableConsumer.close completes.
LOOP · collect again creates a fresh handle
10 · Terminal choice and completion
message.term() or consumer end → Flow completion
Caller-owned term marks an unrecoverable message terminal; normal consumer stop or end-of-stream completes the Flow.
Guardrail · term is not an adapter success signal, and Flow completion is not proof that every business side effect
succeeded.
Next · Return terminal state and metrics to the caller; no hidden ack, retry, or resource ownership remains.
Caller owns policy · adapter owns bounded lifecycle
Adapter-owned boundary · bounded channel / pending observation / handle cleanup ↔ Caller-owned boundary · connection / durable consumer / ack policy / retry
